o.text: From Proto-Oghuz *čigin. Cognate with Turkish çiğin, dialectal Turkish çekin, Turkmen çigin; possibly also cognate with Chuvash ҫан (śan, “body”).
From Russian саксау́л (saksaúl), ultimately from Mongolic, compare Mongolian заг (zag), Kalmyk за (za).
Derivation from Proto-Turkic *uč- (“rash, inflammation, pustules on lips; catarrh, cold, fever; to appear (of rash), catch cold”).
